title: 2 Chronicles 34:29–33
context: Josiah gathers the elders and people, reads the book of the covenant, and makes a covenant before the LORD that the people join. He removes abominations from all Israel’s lands, and throughout his days the people follow the LORD (compare 2 Kings 23:1–3). The account of Josiah continues in chapter 35.

verses.text: Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: The king gathers all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem. Arminian readers see Josiah drawing the nation’s leaders into his response to God’s word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the king leading the people toward covenant renewal. The gathering marks the move from private conviction to public action, as in 2 Kings 23:1.

verses.text: The king went up to the LORD’s house with all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem—the priests, the Levites, and all the people, both great and small—and he read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the LORD’s house.
verses.arminianNotes: The king reads “all the words of the book of the covenant” before the people, “both great and small.” Arminian readers see God’s word made available to everyone.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the public reading as central to renewal. The Chronicler lists “the Levites” where 2 Kings 23:2 has “the prophets,” a difference noted rather than harmonized.

verses.text: The king stood in his place and made a covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD, and to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
verses.arminianNotes: The king makes a covenant “to walk after the LORD … with all his heart and with all his soul.” Arminian readers see a sincere commitment freely made by the king.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see covenant renewal in response to God’s word. The language echoes Deuteronomy’s call to wholehearted love, as in 2 Kings 23:3.

verses.text: He caused all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand. The inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.
verses.arminianNotes: He causes all in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand, and they do “according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.” Arminian readers see the people joining the king’s commitment.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the community brought into the covenant renewal. The Chronicler’s mention of Benjamin reflects his attention to the whole people of God.

verses.text: Josiah took away all the abominations out of all the countries that belonged to the children of Israel, and made all who were found in Israel to serve, even to serve the LORD their God. All his days they didn’t depart from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.arminianNotes: Josiah takes away abominations from all Israel’s lands, and “All his days they didn’t depart from following the LORD.” Arminian readers see faithful leadership producing a season of national faithfulness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the reform completed after the covenant. The note “All his days” is significant, and readers in this tradition see the account of Josiah continuing in chapter 35.
